injuries.description: Tricep muscle — ongoing injury, sidelined for approximately 3 months as of late June 2026 (onset roughly late March 2026; exact date still unconfirmed, carried over from Season 1 rather than a new Season 2 injury).

milestones.description: Beat Chelsea 1-0 at home (MD21); Yacel Amrizi scored from a Rio Ngumoha assist. Liberato Cacace named Man of the Match. Wrexham controlled possession (52% to 48%) for the first time in a long stretch under Jenkins and out-shot Chelsea 5-2 (2.0 xG to 0.3), though finishing in the box remains a work in progress.
Kieffer Moore transferred out to West Brom for £1.5m — last season's Player of the Year, moved on after being transfer-listed as squad talent level rose.
Lost 0-1 away at Brighton (MD20); Al Dawsari's 47th-minute strike settled it. First defeat since Manchester City on 12 December. Wrexham sit 3rd in the Premier League, 42 points from 20 games.

Won 2-1 away at Ipswich Town (MD19); Yacel Amrizi scored and assisted, Leo Sauer added a second after Keillor-Dunn had equalized for Ipswich. Amrizi named Man of the Match. Marco Soria made his senior debut off the bench in the 66th minute, rating 6.8.
Marco Soria (18, LW) and Emiliano Bianchi (17, CDM) promoted from the Youth Academy to the first team. Soria's final academy potential was 74-80 (OVR 67); Bianchi's was 72-76 (OVR 61).

Beat West Ham 2-1 at home on Christmas Day (MD18); Yacel Amrizi and Chido Obi scored either side of half-time after Castellanos had put West Ham ahead early. Brian Gutiérrez, back from his shoulder knock, was named Man of the Match. The win moves Wrexham to 1st in the Premier League table, 39 points from 18 games.
Won 3-1 away at Brentford (MD17); Bobadilla, Obi, and a 90th-minute Sauer penalty saw off a Janelt reply. Brian Gutiérrez picked up a shoulder knock, expected out roughly 4 days.

Wrexham beat a full-strength Manchester City side 2-0 away in the Carabao Cup Quarter Final while fielding a youth-heavy XI, just 3 days after a 1-2 home league defeat to the same club — a statement result for the club. Chido Obi named Man of the Match (1 goal, penalty).

Season 1 (2025-26) archived: journal.html -> journal/season-01.html, season.html -> season/season-01.html, season_log.json -> season_logs/season-01.json. Wrexham AFC finished 1st in the EFL Championship (P46 W36 D4 L6, GF111 GA47, GD+64, 112 pts), automatically promoted. Season 2 begins.
Arthur Okonkwo picked up a tricep muscle injury (~6 weeks), sidelining him early in Season 2 preparations. Mason Webber (17) is next in line in goal.

Danny Ward (32, GK) has submitted a transfer request and is unhappy despite dev being complete at OVR 71 — first squad-management decision of Season 2. Both Ward and Arthur Okonkwo flipped from 'not willing' to 'willing to negotiate new terms' in this review; Mason Webber (17) also now willing to negotiate.

Youth academy roster change — Dijkgraaf and Horne terminated their youth contracts, both wanted out and were not yet good enough for the senior squad. Anton Gassner released from the academy after believing he was good enough for the senior squad — no ultimatums. Added Lenny Kuhn (GK) to the academy.

Danny Ward (32, GK) placed on the transfer list by manager decision — Arthur Okonkwo is returning from injury and Mason Webber (17) is being prioritized for development, leaving Ward surplus to the goalkeeping plans.

Aaron James (20, CB/RB, academy prospect) has submitted a transfer request — contract length demands not met and his deal is down to just 1 month remaining. Needs a squad-management decision (renew, extend, or let him go).

Squad update — Andres Gomez returns from his broken toe injury. Aaron James will not be offered a new contract and will leave as a free agent when his deal expires. The club will try to sign Issa Kabore permanently when his Man City loan expires, though affordability is uncertain. George Dobson transferred out to Besiktas JK for $2.55m. Signed academy goalkeeper (Germany), initially misreported as Lenny Kuhn, then as Finn Richter — real identity confirmed 2026-07-07 as Leo Bergmann.
Signed Chido Obi (18, ST) from the Manchester United academy — a striker prospect, contract accepted with no negotiation friction.

Issa Kabore returned to Manchester City at the end of his loan - the club decided not to pursue a permanent deal. Jay Rodriguez left as a free agent, joining Stade Brestois 29 on the pre-agreed pre-contract move flagged earlier in the summer. Harry Ashfield is back from his Cheltenham Town loan spell. Right-back depth is now thin behind Amelia and A. James.

Signed Jorthy Mokio (18, CDM/CM/LB) from Ajax for £8.7m and Toni Fruk (25, ST/CAM/CM) as a free agent. Fruk slots straight in as the squad's top-rated striker (OVR 79) as Kieffer Moore's decline continues.

Academy: signed 14-year-old French striker Mathieu Drouet (POT 80–94). Also corrected the identity of the German academy goalkeeper signed 2026-06-04 — previously misreported as Lenny Kuhn, then as Finn Richter — the real player is Leo Bergmann (16, POT 71–89).
Alan Minda loaned out to Real Betis (2 years) and Bailey Cadamarteri loaned out to Boca Juniors (12 months). Both recallable early for an agreed fee.
José Luis Rodríguez sold to Al Qadsiah for $6,400,000. Transfer budget now stands at $4,936,320.
Santiago Ortega loaned out to Birmingham City for 12 months, recallable for an agreed fee.

Squad update — Sebastian Revan sold to NEOM SC ($2.0m), Conor Coady sold to RSC Anderlecht ($910k), and Ryan Hardie sold to Leicester City ($1.8m). Signed Jamal Belghazi (17, CDM/CM, being converted to CB) and Mario Barbieri (17, RB) as free agents.
Signed Rio Ngumoha (17, LM/LW) from Liverpool for $22.5m.
Elliot Lee sold to Preston North End ($1.0m).
Ratings / potential reviewed; Roster change
Squad update — signed Andrés Cuenca (19, CB) from Barcelona for $1.9m.
First Premier League match: beat Wolves 2-0 at home. First top-flight win in club history.
Harry Ashfield sold to Silkeborg IF for $580,000.
Paul Mullin sold to Caykur Rizespor ($740K).
Leo Sauer signed from Athletic Bilbao ($22.1m), LW/LM.
George Thomason sold to Club Brugges ($4.1m).

Roster change — Cacace made transition to RB. Next article should do a very deep dive, longer than normal piece based on that every move Wrexham have made this year so far has been with one thing in mind - get younger, get more raw talent. They have made serious investments into the young prodigal player from several world football publications, Jenkins is willing to make a gamble that some of these players turn out to be top class. These same publications have raved at how shrewd of a business man Jenkins has proved to be. Nearly every deal has been under market on buys, and he seems to get the most out of every transfer out. New Academy players from scouting in France and Germany: Stephane Bertrand, Jules Collin, Nico Kopp
Squad update
Ben Sheaf sold to Sunderland (£8.4m).

Transfer window closes. Signed Carlos Macia (CM, 17, from Villarreal, £2.0m) and immediately loaned him to Swansea City for 12 months (70/30 wage split, Wrexham pays 30%). Signed GK Bernt Klaverboer (20, from Burnley, £6.2m) to provide senior cover behind Okonkwo. Sold captain Dominic Hyam to Rangers (£2.6m). Loaned academy GK Mason Webber to Samsunspor for 24 months (70/30 wage split). Window shuts with the club still net spenders across the summer — sustained investment in both first-team depth and academy development pathways is exactly the kind of long-term commitment that tells the Wrexham faithful this club is here to stay.

Wrexham suffer their first Premier League home defeat, 0-2 to Tottenham Hotspur (Kudus 42', 63'). It is the first home league defeat of Jenkins's Wrexham tenure — the club's only previous home loss at the Racecourse came in the Carabao Cup against Blackburn Rovers (27 Aug 2025).
Mo Faal sold to Barracas Central (£1.35m).
Squad update — Cacace signed a new 2-year contract, £44k/week with a £390k signing bonus.
Squad update — Mika Horn (GK, Germany) signed to the Youth Academy; Leo Bergmann and Seun Hak released from the academy.
Fixture reschedule — Manchester City (away) moved from 22 December 2026 to 15 December 2026.
Juan Cruz Vargas (CAM, 17) promoted from the Youth Academy to the first team. Jenkins: "This kid has the potential to be special — I want him getting minutes with the first team now."
Arthur Okonkwo returned from his tricep injury to start in goal against Arsenal (MD12), rating 6.1.
Beat Nottingham Forest 2-0 away; Rio Ngumoha and Juan Cruz Vargas on the scoresheet, Toni Fruk named Man of the Match.
Thrashed Sunderland 5-0 at home; Yacel Amrizi scored a hat-trick (plus an assist) and was named Man of the Match.
Scraped past Leeds United 2-1 away; Yacel Amrizi opened the scoring, Leeds' Joseph equalized late before substitute Juan Cruz Vargas won it in the 88th minute.
Lost 1-2 at home to Manchester City (MD16); Rio Ngumoha's 36th-minute equalizer wasn't enough as Reijnders scored a 90th-minute winner for City.
New Academy signings from scouting in France: Thierry Besse (RW, POT 80-94) and Nathan Salaun (ST, POT 81-87).

Youth Academy Rush Tournament — swept Crystal Palace 3-1, Brentford 4-1, and Wolves 2-0 in a single-day event to win the tournament. Nico Kopp was Man of the Match in both the semi-final (9.8 rating) and the final (7.8 rating); Valentino Martini scored a hat-trick plus an assist in the semi-final.

Transfer window opened: Thiago Pitarch (19, CM/CDM/CAM, OVR 73) signed from Real Madrid for CM depth — fee not disclosed, $52K/w wage, 4y6m contract, Rotation squad role. Kieffer Moore transfer-listed — last season's Player of the Year, but now surplus as squad talent level has risen. Andrés Cuenca, Joenathan Amelia, and Marco Soria (newly promoted) loan-listed to get more first-team minutes.
